title: A Note on the formulation of the Neumann boundary condition for a nonlocal problem: the measure-preserving outer-collar involution (printed as Theorem 2.5)
author: Antonio Luiz Pereira
work: A Note on the formulation of the Neumann boundary condition for a nonlocal problem
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Theorem 2.5 (source0.tex lines 390--400, source label area_preserving), the existence of an epsilon-collar map from the inner collar of the domain onto an open subset of the exterior that is a homeomorphism, preserves Lebesgue measure, extends to an involution and has Jacobian determinant minus one. It is the construction on which the note's reformulation of the Neumann condition rests, and it is delivered with the article's complete original proof at source0.tex lines 402--453 (52 lines, the article's own run-in proof block from the marker to the closing square). The proof is a genuine construction: it first computes the Jacobian of the normal-coordinate parametrisation by diagonalising the shape operator and obtains the normal-coordinate integration formula with the weight p_y(s); it then defines the height function by a separable ordinary differential equation, solves it explicitly through the primitive P_y and its inverse, and uses continuity and compactness of the boundary to show that the solution is defined on a uniform collar and is an involution; it then builds the map from the height function, proves it is a homeomorphism onto a set that contains the outer collar of depth epsilon prime, transfers the measure-preservation statement through the change of variables solving the differential equation, and finally computes the determinant of the derivative as minus one from the block-triangular structure of the derivative of the normal-coordinate map. The substantive steps are the explicit solution of the height equation, the uniform-collar estimate and the determinant computation; none of them is an unpacking of definitions. H2: a complete original research-paper theorem, moderately short, whose proof is a genuinely technical construction rather than a routine verification.
